description: The SECOND COMPOUND CASE of this folder, and the one that proves CBTRN01C's two read-status flags are RE-INITIALISED on every iteration rather than latched across them: the account miss lands on the LAST record, so the post-end-of-file pass resolves the cross reference and then fails the account read A SECOND TIME. It composes three behaviours each already pinned separately - the clean hit of case01, the post-end-of-file lookup of case04 and the account-miss vocabulary and message ordering of case08 - and the vocabulary of all three is reused verbatim rather than restated. WHAT THE TWO RE-INITIALISATIONS DO. app/cbl/CBTRN01C.cbl:170 moves 0 into WS-XREF-READ-STATUS and :174 moves 0 into WS-ACCT-READ-STATUS, and BOTH sit outside the inner guard that opens at :167 and closes at :169 - a guard covering ONLY the record echo at :168 - so both run on every iteration including the one whose READ reported end of file. On that trailing pass the cross-reference lookup is therefore a FRESH attempt against the stale DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM the last record left in WORKING-STORAGE, and it succeeds because that card is resolvable; WS-ACCT-READ-STATUS is reset to 0, the keyed account read at :243 is a FRESH attempt, and it takes the INVALID KEY phrase again; so the mainline test at :177 fires again and :178 emits the account-not-found line a second time. Were either flag latched instead of reset - carrying 4 forward from the previous iteration - the trailing block would come out with the wrong shape: a latched WS-XREF-READ-STATUS would fail the test at :173 and divert to the ELSE at :180, and a latched WS-ACCT-READ-STATUS would report a miss the read never performed. Detecting exactly that is why this case exists. THE TRAILING BLOCK IS SIX LINES, NOT FIVE, and this is stated explicitly because a reader who has seen case01 or case12 will reasonably expect five (practice B8). In those cases the trailing account read SUCCEEDS and contributes ONE line, the success line at :249, giving four lookup lines plus one. Here it FAILS and contributes TWO, :246 and :178, giving four lookup lines plus two. The arithmetic of the whole run is therefore 1 banner + 6 for the first record (echo, four lookup lines, one account success) + 7 for the second (echo, four lookup lines, two account-miss lines) + 6 for the post-end-of-file pass (four lookup lines, two account-miss lines, and NO echo) + 1 banner = TWENTY-ONE lines. A run performs recordsRead + 1 lookups always; with two records that is three, and entries 3-6, 9-12 and 15-18 are those three lookups. TWO ORDERINGS THIS CASE PINS, BOTH TWICE. First, :246 ALWAYS PRECEDES :178. 3000-READ-ACCOUNT at :241-250 takes its INVALID KEY phrase and displays 'INVALID ACCOUNT NUMBER FOUND' at :246 from inside the paragraph, then moves 4 into WS-ACCT-READ-STATUS at :247; only after the PERFORM at :176 has returned does the mainline test that flag at :177 and display 'ACCOUNT ' ACCT-ID ' NOT FOUND' at :178. So entry 13 is :246 and entry 14 is :178, and entries 19 and 20 repeat that pair in the same order - stated explicitly rather than left to intuition, and asserted at both sites rather than only the first. Second, THERE IS NO RECORD ECHO BETWEEN ENTRY 14 AND ENTRY 15. The READ at :203 reported '10', the ladder at :204-212 moved 16 into APPL-RESULT at :208, 16 matches the 88 APPL-EOF condition declared at :144 and :217 moved 'Y' into END-OF-DAILY-TRANS-FILE, so the guard at :167 suppresses the DISPLAY at :168 - and only that. Entries 15-20 are therefore element-wise identical to entries 9-14 with the echo removed from the front. The trailing block and the duplicated account-miss report are ASSERTED RATHER THAN TRIMMED, DE-DUPLICATED OR ESCALATED TO AN ABEND, because they are what the source does and a like-for-like migration reproduces behaviour exactly as found: hoisting :170-172 inside the guard, collapsing the two identical account-miss pairs into one, or promoting the local flag value 4 into a non-zero return code each makes this case fail, which is exactly the point (practice B5). WHY ACCT-ID IS STILL POPULATED AT :178, at both sites. :175 moved XREF-ACCT-ID into ACCT-ID before the read, and READ ... RECORD INTO ACCOUNT-RECORD does not disturb its receiving area when the INVALID KEY phrase runs, so ACCT-ID still holds the cross reference's own account id. It renders as ELEVEN ZERO-PADDED DIGITS because ACCT-ID is PIC 9(11) at bytes 1-11 of app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy, as XREF-ACCT-ID is at bytes 26-36 of app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy; the eleven-digit rendering follows from the PICTURE clause and not from a formatting choice (practice B11). The line is one DISPLAY of two literals around one operand and COBOL adds no separator of its own, so 'ACCOUNT ' + 00000000020 + ' NOT FOUND' is exactly the twenty-nine characters of entries 14 and 20. The lookup lines are read the same way: :237's literal is 'ACCOUNT ID : ' and carries a SPACE BEFORE THE COLON, which :236's 'CARD NUMBER: ' and :238's 'CUSTOMER ID: ' do not. HOW THE MISS IS MANUFACTURED. All fifty cross-referenced accounts are present in the full acctdata.txt, so the miss cannot come from the fixture as a whole and MUST NOT come from editing it. ACCTFILE is therefore seeded with a REDUCED SUBSET - acctdata.txt row 7 (zero-based 6) alone, the row holding account 00000000007 - and acctdata.txt ROW 20 IS DELIBERATELY OMITTED. Row 20 is the ONLY row of that fixture whose first eleven bytes are 00000000020, which is verified programmatically rather than assumed, so its omission makes the miss STRUCTURAL: there is no row the keyed read at :243 could have matched. app/data/ASCII is not modified in any way, because it is the only oracle this migration has (practice B3). Seeding one real row rather than an empty dataset is what makes this a genuine key miss against non-empty data rather than an end-of-file on an empty file, and it is also what lets the FIRST record hit while the second misses. THE SEEDS, AND WHY THE SECOND RECORD IS THE LAST ONE. DALYTRAN carries dailytran.txt rows 1 and 2 in that order. Row 1 is DALYTRAN-ID 0000000000683580 whose DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM at bytes 263-278 of app/cpy/CVTRA06Y.cpy is 4859452612877065; row 2 is DALYTRAN-ID 0000000001774260 whose card is 0927987108636232. XREFFILE carries cardxref.txt rows 21 and 4, and BOTH MUST RESOLVE for this case to mean what it says: row 21 maps 4859452612877065 to customer 000000007 and account 00000000007, which the seeded ACCTFILE row satisfies, and row 4 maps 0927987108636232 to customer 000000020 and account 00000000020, which it does not. Because record 2 is the LAST record, the card the trailing pass reuses is the card of the record that MISSED - which is the whole point, and what distinguishes this case from case08, where the single record's miss is repeated with nothing after it, and from case12, where two clean records are followed by a clean repeat. THREE LINES ARE ABSENT FROM THIS CASE AND THEIR ABSENCE IS DELIBERATE, each cited by source line rather than quoted so that a reviewer's plain search over this file for any of them returns nothing (practice B11): the INVALID KEY line of 2000-LOOKUP-XREF at :232 and the four-operand skip line the ELSE arm displays at :181-183, both of which belong to a cross reference that did NOT resolve and neither of which is reached here because both cross references DO resolve; and the success line of 3000-READ-ACCOUNT at :249, which appears exactly ONCE - for record 1 - and not for record 2 nor for the trailing pass. RETURN CODE 0, stated explicitly and never defaulted. An account miss is a normal, non-abending outcome: :247 moves 4 into WS-ACCT-READ-STATUS, which is a LOCAL FLAG the mainline reads at :177 and nothing else. CBTRN01C contains no MOVE statement targeting RETURN-CODE anywhere, and the CALL 'CEE3ABD' at :473 is reachable only from an open, close or non-end-of-file read failure and is unreached here, so the flag value 4 must NOT be promoted into the return code and 0 is the only right answer. NOTHING IS WRITTEN, asserted positively rather than by absence of interest. expectedWrites is empty because a scan of the source finds zero WRITE and zero REWRITE statements and all six files are OPEN INPUT, and the six writes-channel dataset expectations below say the same thing per dataset at its exact copybook width - including CUSTFILE, CARDFILE and TRANFILE, which :158-160 open and :189-191 close but which no READ in this program ever touches, the only reads being DALYTRAN at :203, XREF-FILE at :229 and ACCOUNT-FILE at :243. Those three are declared with the empty shape - "empty": true with their declared 500-, 150- and 350-byte widths and their CVCUS01Y, CVACT02Y and CVTRA05Y copybooks - which positively states that each exists and holds no row, and they are pinned at zero rows on the final-state channel as well. WIDTHS AND FILLER. The two daily rows are pinned unchanged on the final-state channel at the full 350 bytes CVTRA06Y declares. The cross-reference rows are seeded at the 36 bytes cardxref.txt actually holds and are NOT pre-padded; the declared CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation supplies CVACT03Y's absent FILLER X(14) once, at seed time, before anything decodes a row, and the final state pins all four spans of both rows by name - 16 + 9 + 11 + 14 = the whole 50 bytes, so no byte goes unasserted (gate G16, risk R-F). The account row is pinned at its full 300 bytes, whose CVACT01Y FILLER X(178) is space-filled across bytes 123-300 and whose ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE keeps the copybook's own misspelling (requirement I1); pinning the total width is what proves every FILLER span was emitted, since a record missing one is short by exactly that span (gates G19 and G21). ACCT-ID is additionally pinned by name at 00000000007 so that the identity of the row that IS seeded - and therefore the identity of the one that is not - is legible in the expectation and not only in the seed. R1 AND PRACTICE B4, documented and not 'fixed'. The mandated class name TransactionPostingJob and the source header 'Post the records from daily transaction file' both promise posting, and the verified source posts nothing at all. CBTRN01C is also this migration's orphan, invoked by no EXEC PGM= in app/jcl or app/proc, so jobParameters is empty because there is no PARM for one to come from and the job carries no trigger (gate G13, requirement I4). A second divergence is recorded here for the same reason rather than absorbed silently: the in-code scenario of THIS ordinal in CBTRN01CParityTest is an OPEN FAILURE of the account file, and an open failure is INEXPRESSIBLE as a declarative fixture. It is driven by an Injection, which is a member of that class's own ParityScenario wrapper and not of ParityCase; the only forced-outcome mechanism ParityCase offers is a screenRequest member, and a BATCH_JOB case must leave screenRequest absent. So the open-failure ordinals cannot be written as JSON at all, and this fixture pins the seed-driven compound behaviour the model DOES express - the same resolution case08 records for its own ordinal, reached independently and by the same reasoning. Neither the test class nor any COBOL source is modified to reconcile the two. BASELINE PROVENANCE, practice B12. These expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from app/cbl/CBTRN01C.cbl :164-186 and :241-250 read statement by statement, cross-checked against the copybook byte layouts in app/cpy (CVTRA06Y 350, CVACT03Y 50, CVACT01Y 300, every offset mechanically diffable by eye) and against the real ASCII fixtures named above - dailytran.txt rows 1 and 2, cardxref.txt rows 21 and 4, and acctdata.txt row 7, every one of which is read verbatim from app/data/ASCII rather than retyped, with acctdata.txt row 20 omitted deliberately. They were NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL, because executing it is empirically impossible in this environment - no z/OS or CICS runtime, an indexed-file handler the available compiler reports as disabled, and no Language Environment CEE* services. AAP section 0.7.6 records eight independently verified blockers; the substitution changes the PROVENANCE of the expected values and nothing else, and is escalated for explicit user confirmation as risk R-A rather than silently absorbed. Bytes are US-ASCII, stated and never taken from the platform default, and nothing here reads a clock, draws an unpredictable value or consults the environment - CBTRN01C reads no clock, so the fingerprint is identical on every run (practices B7 and B8). review_rules returns exactly one line, "No user rules provided.", so no user rule governs this fixture; the binding standard is the enterprise-practice set, and its absence is not licence to assert less. Both 350-character record images and all twenty-one message entries are written out in full, with no abbreviation, no elision and nothing left standing in for a value that a later pass would have to supply (practice B1). Gates carried: G13, G15, G16, G18, G19, G21, G30 (the IF at :177 judged twice, and both READ arm pairs - :231-238 and :245-249 - in source order), G47 ('00' at the cross-reference site TWICE, '00' then '23' TWICE at the account site, and '10' at the sequential read) and G51 (the tasklet body is driven directly, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP layer in the path). G32 does not apply: CBTRN01C contains zero GO TO statements.
